function.name: has_extension
function.description: This function checks if a given string (list) contains a specific extension (ext).

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: This is the string where the function will look for the extension.

parameters.name: ext
parameters.description: This is the extension that the function will look for in the string.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the extension is found in the string, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: dump_extensions
function.description: This function iterates over a list of extensions and prints them. If an extension is longer than 128 characters, it only prints the first 128 characters.

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: A string containing a list of extensions separated by spaces.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything

function.name: register_extension
function.description: This function registers an extension if it does not already exist in the list. It adds the extension to the list, separated by a space if the list is not empty.

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: A list of extensions

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The size of the list

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the extension to be registered

function.return_type: void, this function does not return any value

function.name: opengl_drawable_create
function.description: This function creates an OpenGL drawable object, initializes its properties, and returns a pointer to it.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The size of the drawable object to be created.

parameters.name: funcs
parameters.description: Pointer to the structure containing the function pointers for the drawable object.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: The pixel format of the drawable object.

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: Pointer to the client surface where the drawable object will be created.

function.return_type: void *: Returns a pointer to the created opengl_drawable object. Returns NULL if the object could not be created.

function.name: opengl_drawable_add_ref
function.description: This function increments the reference count of the opengl_drawable object.

parameters.name: drawable
parameters.description: This is the opengl_drawable object whose reference count is to be incremented.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return any value.

function.name: opengl_drawable_release
function.description: This function decreases the reference count of the opengl_drawable object. If the reference count reaches zero, it destroys the drawable, releases the client surface if it exists, and frees the memory allocated to the drawable.

parameters.name: drawable
parameters.description: A pointer to the opengl_drawable object whose reference count is to be decreased.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything

function.name: opengl_drawable_set_context
function.description: This function sets the context for the given OpenGL drawable. If the context is not null, it sets the driver_private of the context to the drawable's set_context function.

parameters.name: drawable
parameters.description: This is the OpenGL drawable whose context is to be set.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: This is the context to be set. If it is not null, its driver_private is used.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything.

function.name: opengl_drawable_flush
function.description: This function flushes the OpenGL drawable object. It checks if the client surface window is not null, updates the drawable object if necessary, sets the interval, and finally calls the flush function of the drawable object if certain conditions are met.

parameters.name: drawable
parameters.description: This is the OpenGL drawable object that is to be flushed.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: This parameter represents the interval at which the drawable object is to be flushed.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: This parameter is used for setting various flags that control the behavior of the flush operation.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything.

function.name: opengl_drawable_swap
function.description: This function checks if the client surface window is valid, if not, it returns FALSE. If it is valid, it calls the swap function of the drawable object.

parameters.name: drawable
parameters.description: This parameter is a pointer to an opengl_drawable structure. It is used to access the client and funcs properties of the drawable object.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the swap operation was successful or not

function.name: read_drm_device_prop
function.description: This function reads a property of a DRM device by opening a file in the sysfs interface, reading the property value, and returning it.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the DRM device.

parameters.name: prop
parameters.description: The property of the DRM device to read.

function.return_type: UINT, represents the value of the requested property of the DRM device. Returns -1 if the property cannot be read.

function.name: init_device_info
function.description: This function initializes the device information. It sets up the versions, contexts, extensions, configurations, and other properties related to the device. It also handles the creation and destruction of contexts.

parameters.name: egl
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the egl platform structure which contains information about the egl platform.

parameters.name: funcs
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the opengl functions structure which contains function pointers to opengl functions.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything as it modifies the input structures in place.

function.name: nulldrv_get_proc_address
function.description: This function returns NULL for a given name

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: This parameter represents the name for which the function returns NULL

function.return_type: void *: represents a pointer to the return type of the function

function.name: nulldrv_init_pixel_formats
function.description: This function initializes the pixel formats for the null driver by setting the onscreen_count to the size of the nulldrv_pixel_formats array and returning the same value.

parameters.name: onscreen_count
parameters.description: Pointer to a UINT variable where the function will store the size of the nulldrv_pixel_formats array.

function.return_type: UINT, representing the size of the nulldrv_pixel_formats array

function.name: nulldrv_describe_pixel_format
function.description: This function describes the pixel format by setting the properties of the 'descr' parameter based on the 'format' parameter. It returns FALSE if the 'format' is out of range, otherwise it returns TRUE after successfully setting the properties.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: This parameter is used to determine the pixel format to be described.

parameters.name: descr
parameters.description: This parameter is a pointer to a struct that will be filled with the details of the pixel format.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the pixel format was successfully described or not.

function.name: nulldrv_init_wgl_extensions
function.description: This function initializes WGL extensions in the Null driver.

parameters.name: funcs
parameters.description: Pointer to the opengl_funcs structure

function.return_type: char: Returns an empty string

function.name: nulldrv_surface_create
function.description: This function is used to create a surface with null driver.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to a window

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Format of the surface to be created

parameters.name: drawable
parameters.description: Pointer to a pointer of opengl_drawable structure

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE indicating successful creation of surface

function.name: nulldrv_pbuffer_create
function.description: This function is used to create a null driver pixel buffer but always returns FALSE indicating failure.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to the device context

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Specifies the pixel format

parameters.name: largest
parameters.description: Indicates whether to create the largest pbuffer possible

parameters.name: texture_format
parameters.description: Specifies the texture format

parameters.name: texture_target
parameters.description: Specifies the texture target

parameters.name: max_level
parameters.description: Specifies the maximum level of detail for the texture

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Pointer to the width of the pbuffer

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Pointer to the height of the pbuffer

parameters.name: drawable
parameters.description: Pointer to the opengl drawable structure

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the pbuffer was successfully created or not

function.name: nulldrv_pbuffer_updated
function.description: This function returns a boolean value indicating the status of the pbuffer update in the null driver.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to the device context.

parameters.name: drawable
parameters.description: Pointer to the OpenGL drawable structure.

parameters.name: cube_face
parameters.description: Enumeration value representing the cube face.

parameters.name: mipmap_level
parameters.description: Integer representing the mipmap level.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the pbuffer update in the null driver was successful or not.

function.name: nulldrv_pbuffer_bind
function.description: This function is used to bind a pbuffer to a drawable object. It returns -1 to use the default implementation.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to the device context.

parameters.name: drawable
parameters.description: Pointer to the drawable object.

parameters.name: buffer
parameters.description: Specifies the buffer to bind.

function.return_type: UINT, represents the status of the binding operation. Returns -1 to use the default implementation.

function.name: nulldrv_context_create
function.description: This function is used to create a context in the null driver. However, it always returns FALSE, indicating that the context creation was unsuccessful.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: This parameter is used to specify the format.

parameters.name: share
parameters.description: This parameter is used to share data across different contexts.

parameters.name: attribs
parameters.description: This parameter is used to specify the attributes.

parameters.name: private
parameters.description: This parameter is used to store private data.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the context creation was successful or not. In this case, it always returns FALSE.

function.name: nulldrv_context_destroy
function.description: This function is used to destroy a null driver context.

parameters.name: private
parameters.description: This parameter is a pointer to the private context to be destroyed.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the context was successfully destroyed. In this case, it always returns FALSE, indicating failure.

function.name: nulldrv_make_current
function.description: This function is used to set the current OpenGL drawable objects, but it always returns FALSE indicating that the operation was not successful.

parameters.name: draw_base
parameters.description: This parameter is used to specify the base drawable object for drawing operations.

parameters.name: read_base
parameters.description: This parameter is used to specify the base drawable object for reading operations.

parameters.name: private
parameters.description: This parameter is used to pass any additional private data required by the function.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the operation was successful or not. In this case, it always returns FALSE.

function.name: win32u_wglGetExtensionsStringARB
function.description: This function returns the extensions of the wgl. It first traces the hdc, checks if the trace is on wgl, and then dumps the wgl extensions.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to a device context.

function.return_type: char: Returns the wgl extensions.

function.name: win32u_wglGetExtensionsStringEXT
function.description: This function returns the extensions of the wgl. It first traces and then dumps the extensions if the trace is on. Finally, it returns the wgl extensions.
function.return_type: char: This represents the wgl extensions that the function returns.

function.name: get_dc_pixel_format
function.description: This function retrieves the pixel format for a device context or a window. If the handle is invalid, it sets the last error to ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE and returns -1. If the pixel format is offscreen and can't be used with traditional WGL calls, it returns 1.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to the device context.

parameters.name: internal
parameters.description: Boolean value that indicates whether the pixel format is internal or not.

function.return_type: int, represents the pixel format of the device context or window. Returns -1 if the handle is invalid, 1 if the pixel format is offscreen and can't be used with traditional WGL calls.

function.name: win32u_wglGetPixelFormat
function.description: This function gets the pixel format of a device context.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: This parameter is a handle to the device context.

function.return_type: int, represents the pixel format of the device context. If the format is not greater than 0, it returns 0.

function.name: set_window_opengl_drawable
function.description: This function sets the OpenGL drawable for a window, either as the current drawable or as an unused drawable. It also manages the reference count of the drawable objects.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window for which the OpenGL drawable is to be set.

parameters.name: new_drawable
parameters.description: Pointer to the new OpenGL drawable to be set for the window.

parameters.name: current
parameters.description: Boolean value indicating whether the new drawable is to be set as the current drawable. If false, the new drawable is set as an unused drawable.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value.

function.name: get_window_current_drawable
function.description: This function retrieves the current drawable object associated with a given window handle.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window for which the current drawable object is to be retrieved.

function.return_type: struct opengl_drawable*; it represents a pointer to the current drawable object associated with the window. If no such object exists, the function returns NULL.

function.name: get_window_unused_drawable
function.description: This function retrieves an unused drawable from a window if available. If not, it creates a new one. It also ensures that the drawable format matches the requested format.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window from which to retrieve the unused drawable.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: The desired format of the drawable.

function.return_type: struct opengl_drawable*, represents the unused drawable from the window or a newly created one if no unused drawable was available.

function.name: set_dc_opengl_drawable
function.description: This function sets a new OpenGL drawable for a device context, releases the old drawable if it exists, and adds a reference to the new drawable.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: This is a handle to the device context.

parameters.name: new_drawable
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the new OpenGL drawable to be set.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value.

function.name: get_dc_opengl_drawable
function.description: This function retrieves the opengl_drawable from the device context if it exists, adds a reference to it, and then releases the device context. It then returns the opengl_drawable.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: This is a handle to the device context.

function.return_type: struct opengl_drawable*, represents the opengl_drawable retrieved from the device context.

function.name: create_memory_pbuffer
function.description: This function creates a pixel buffer for memory device context. It checks if the device context is valid, if it's drawable, and if it's a memory device context. If all checks pass, it gets the bitmap associated with the device context, initializes a DIB (Device Independent Bitmap) from the bitmap, and releases the bitmap. If the pixel format is valid, it creates a pixel buffer and sets it as the drawable for the device context, and then destroys the pixel buffer.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to the device context for which the pixel buffer is to be created.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the pixel buffer is successfully created, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: flush_memory_dc
function.description: This function is used to flush the memory device context. It checks the type of GDI object, gets the image from the bitmap, and then either draws or reads pixels based on the 'write' parameter. It also releases the DC pointer at the end.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Pointer to the wgl_context structure

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to the device context

parameters.name: write
parameters.description: Flag to determine whether to draw or read pixels

parameters.name: flush
parameters.description: Pointer to the function to flush the memory

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the function was successful or not

function.name: set_dc_pixel_format
function.description: This function sets the pixel format for a device context. It first checks if the new format is valid. If it is, it gets the window associated with the device context. If the window exists, it sets the pixel format for the window. If the window does not exist, it sets the pixel format for the device context.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: This is the handle to the device context for which the pixel format is to be set.

parameters.name: new_format
parameters.description: This is the new pixel format to be set.

parameters.name: internal
parameters.description: This parameter is used to determine whether the function should return the old format if it exists and is not internal.

function.return_type: BOOL, it represents whether the pixel format was successfully set or not.

function.name: win32u_wglSetPixelFormat
function.description: This function sets the pixel format of the specified device context.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to the device context.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Specifies the index number of the pixel format to be set.

parameters.name: pfd
parameters.description: Pointer to a PIXELFORMATDESCRIPTOR structure that contains the logical pixel format specification.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the pixel format was set successfully; otherwise, it returns FALSE.

function.name: win32u_wglSetPixelFormatWINE
function.description: This function sets the pixel format of the specified device context.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: This is a handle to the device context.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: This specifies the pixel format to be set.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the pixel format was set successfully, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: win32u_wglGetProcAddress
function.description: This function checks if the input string starts with 'wgl'. If it does, it returns NULL. Otherwise, it gets the address of the procedure specified by the name and returns it.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the procedure for which the address is to be retrieved.

function.return_type: PROC, which represents the address of the procedure specified by the name parameter. If the name starts with 'wgl', NULL is returned.

function.name: win32u_get_pixel_formats
function.description: This function copies pixel formats into a provided buffer, and sets the number of formats and onscreen formats.

parameters.name: formats
parameters.description: Pointer to a buffer where the pixel formats will be copied.

parameters.name: max_formats
parameters.description: The maximum number of pixel formats that can be copied into the buffer.

parameters.name: num_formats
parameters.description: Pointer to a variable where the function will store the total number of pixel formats.

parameters.name: num_onscreen_formats
parameters.description: Pointer to a variable where the function will store the number of onscreen pixel formats.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value

function.name: context_exchange_drawables
function.description: This function exchanges the draw and read pointers in the given context with the provided new draw and read pointers.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Pointer to the context where the draw and read pointers are to be exchanged.

parameters.name: draw
parameters.description: Pointer to the new draw pointer to be set in the context.

parameters.name: read
parameters.description: Pointer to the new read pointer to be set in the context.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value

function.name: context_unset_current
function.description: This function unsets the current context and then resets it, possibly to a different context. It also handles the case where the draw and read contexts are different.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: The context to be unset and then reset.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the driver's current context is successfully unset, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: get_updated_drawable
function.description: This function updates the drawable object based on the given HDC and format. If the window still has a drawable, it keeps using the one it has. Otherwise, it gets an updated drawable with the desired format.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to a device context.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Format to be used for the drawable.

parameters.name: drawable
parameters.description: Pointer to the drawable object to be updated.

function.return_type: struct opengl_drawable *: Returns an updated drawable object based on the given HDC and format. If the window still has a drawable, it returns the existing one. If not, it returns a new drawable with the desired format.

function.name: context_sync_drawables
function.description: This function synchronizes the drawables in a given context, updates the current window drawable to the last used draw surface, and manages the ownership of the previous context drawables.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: This is the context in which the drawables are to be synchronized.

parameters.name: draw_hdc
parameters.description: This is the device context for the drawable to be drawn.

parameters.name: read_hdc
parameters.description: This is the device context for the drawable to be read.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the synchronization was successful, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: push_internal_context
function.description: This function creates an internal context if it does not exist and makes it the current context.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Pointer to a wgl_context structure

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to a device context

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Format to be used for creating the context

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything

function.name: pop_internal_context
function.description: This function is used to make the current context for the given draw, read, and driver_private fields of the passed wgl_context structure.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: This parameter is a pointer to a wgl_context structure. It is used to access the draw, read, and driver_private fields within the function.

function.return_type: void, which means this function does not return a value

function.name: win32u_wglMakeContextCurrentARB
function.description: This function is used to make a specified OpenGL rendering context the calling thread's current rendering context. All subsequent OpenGL calls made by the thread are drawn on the context identified by 'context'. It also checks the validity of the pixel format of the draw_hdc and the format of the context, and sets the error if they are invalid or mismatched.

parameters.name: draw_hdc
parameters.description: Handle to a device context for the device on which the drawing is to be rendered.

parameters.name: read_hdc
parameters.description: Handle to a device context for the device from which the pixels are to be read.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Pointer to a 'wgl_context' structure that specifies the OpenGL rendering context.

function.return_type: BOOL, where TRUE indicates that the function succeeded in making the specified OpenGL rendering context the calling thread's current rendering context, and FALSE indicates that the function failed.

function.name: win32u_wglMakeCurrent
function.description: This function makes a specified OpenGL context the calling thread's current rendering context.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to a device context.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Pointer to a wgl_context structure.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the function was successful in making the specified OpenGL context the current rendering context.

function.name: win32u_wglCreatePbufferARB
function.description: This function creates a pixel buffer and sets its properties based on the provided attributes. It also handles error checking for invalid parameters and system resource availability.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to a device context.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Specifies the pixel format.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Specifies the width of the pixel buffer.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Specifies the height of the pixel buffer.

parameters.name: attribs
parameters.description: Pointer to an array of attributes for the pixel buffer.

function.return_type: struct wgl_pbuffer *; Returns a pointer to a wgl_pbuffer structure if successful, otherwise NULL.

function.name: win32u_wglDestroyPbufferARB
function.description: This function releases the opengl drawable, deletes the object application associated with the pbuffer's device context handle, and frees the memory allocated to the pbuffer. It then returns GL_TRUE.

parameters.name: pbuffer
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the wgl_pbuffer structure that is to be destroyed.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the function executed successfully. Returns GL_TRUE after successful execution.

function.name: win32u_wglGetPbufferDCARB
function.description: This function returns the device context handle associated with the given pixel buffer.

parameters.name: pbuffer
parameters.description: A pointer to the pixel buffer whose device context handle is to be retrieved.

function.return_type: HDC, which represents the device context handle associated with the given pixel buffer.

function.name: win32u_wglReleasePbufferDCARB
function.description: This function checks if the given device context (hdc) matches the one in the provided wgl_pbuffer structure. If not, it sets the last Win32 error to ERROR_DC_NOT_FOUND and returns FALSE. Otherwise, it returns TRUE.

parameters.name: pbuffer
parameters.description: Pointer to a wgl_pbuffer structure

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to a device context

function.return_type: int, returns TRUE if the hdc matches the one in the pbuffer structure, otherwise returns FALSE

function.name: win32u_wglQueryPbufferARB
function.description: This function queries the properties of a pbuffer. The queried property is determined by the 'attrib' parameter, and the result is stored in the 'value' parameter.

parameters.name: pbuffer
parameters.description: A pointer to the pbuffer to be queried.

parameters.name: attrib
parameters.description: The attribute of the pbuffer to be queried. This can be one of several predefined constants.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: A pointer to an integer where the result of the query will be stored.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns GL_TRUE on successful execution.

function.name: binding_from_target
function.description: This function returns the binding constant associated with the given texture target. If the target is not supported, it logs an error and returns 0.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: This is the texture target for which the binding constant is to be returned.

function.return_type: GLenum, represents the binding constant associated with the given texture target. Returns 0 if the target is not supported.

function.name: win32u_wglBindTexImageARB
function.description: This function binds a texture image to a pbuffer. It handles different types of source buffers and sets the appropriate OpenGL source. It also handles errors and sets the last Win32 error accordingly.

parameters.name: pbuffer
parameters.description: A pointer to the pbuffer to which the texture image will be bound.

parameters.name: buffer
parameters.description: The buffer type. It determines the source buffer to be used in the binding process.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the binding was successful or not. It returns GL_FALSE if there was an error, and GL_TRUE if the binding was successful.

function.name: win32u_wglReleaseTexImageARB
function.description: This function releases a texture image from a pbuffer and returns a boolean value indicating the success or failure of the operation.

parameters.name: pbuffer
parameters.description: A pointer to the pbuffer from which the texture image is to be released.

parameters.name: buffer
parameters.description: An integer representing the buffer.

function.return_type: BOOL, where TRUE indicates that the operation was successful and FALSE indicates that it failed.

function.name: win32u_wglSetPbufferAttribARB
function.description: This function sets the attributes of a pixel buffer. It checks the texture format of the pixel buffer and sets the last win32 error if it's invalid. It then loops through the attributes and sets the mipmap level and cube face based on the attribute values. If an invalid attribute or unknown texture face is encountered, it sets the last win32 error and returns false. Finally, it calls the pbuffer updated function of the driver functions with the pixel buffer's device context, drawable, cube face, and maximum of mipmap level and 0.

parameters.name: pbuffer
parameters.description: Pointer to the pixel buffer whose attributes are to be set

parameters.name: attribs
parameters.description: Pointer to the array of attributes to be set for the pixel buffer

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the attributes were successfully set or not

function.name: get_window_swap_interval
function.description: This function retrieves the swap interval of a window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window whose swap interval is to be retrieved.

function.return_type: int, represents the swap interval of the window. If the window pointer is not found, or the window is a desktop or another process, it returns 0.

function.name: win32u_wgl_context_reset
function.description: This function resets the given WGL context. If the context has an internal context or a driver private, it destroys them. If a device context handle is provided, it creates a new driver context for the given WGL context.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: The WGL context to be reset.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to a device context. If not NULL, a new driver context is created for the WGL context.

parameters.name: share
parameters.description: The WGL context to share resources with. If not NULL, its driver private is used when creating a new driver context.

parameters.name: attribs
parameters.description: Pointer to an array of attributes for the new driver context.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully resets the WGL context, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: flush_memory_pbuffer
function.description: This function creates a memory pbuffer, syncs drawables if a context exists, flushes memory DC if created, and finally flushes memory DC with the provided flush function.

parameters.name: flush
parameters.description: This is a function pointer to a function that takes no parameters and returns no value. It is used to flush the memory DC.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the memory DC was successfully flushed or not.

function.name: win32u_wgl_context_flush
function.description: This function is used to flush the given OpenGL context, potentially forcing a buffer swap.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: The OpenGL context to be flushed.

parameters.name: flush
parameters.description: A pointer to a function that will be called to perform the actual flushing operation.

parameters.name: force_swap
parameters.description: A boolean value that, if true, forces a buffer swap after the flush operation.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE always indicating the successful execution of the function.

function.name: win32u_wglSwapBuffers
function.description: This function handles the swapping of buffers in a Windows OpenGL context. It retrieves the current OpenGL context, checks the swap interval for the window, and then either syncs the drawables if a context exists or gets the current drawable for the window. It then flushes the drawable, swaps the drawable, and releases the drawable.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to the device context for the window where the buffers are to be swapped.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the buffer swap was successful or not.

function.name: win32u_wglSwapIntervalEXT
function.description: This function sets the swap interval for a window. It first retrieves the device context for the current thread and the window associated with it. If it fails to find either, it sets the last error to ERROR_DC_NOT_FOUND and returns FALSE. If the window is the desktop or belongs to another process, it logs a warning and returns TRUE. Otherwise, it sets the swap interval for the window, releases the window pointer, and returns TRUE.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: The swap interval to set for the window.

function.return_type: BOOL, representing whether the operation was successful. Returns FALSE if the device context or window could not be found, TRUE otherwise.

function.name: win32u_wglGetSwapIntervalEXT
function.description: This function retrieves the swap interval for the current OpenGL rendering context. It handles errors and warnings related to the window and the device context.

parameters.name: void
parameters.description: This function does not accept any parameters.

function.return_type: int, represents the swap interval for the current OpenGL rendering context. If an error occurs, it returns 0 or TRUE depending on the error.

function.name: win32u_wglQueryRendererIntegerWINE
function.description: This function queries the renderer for various attributes and returns the value in the 'value' parameter. It also checks if the renderer is within the range of available devices.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to the device context.

parameters.name: renderer
parameters.description: The index of the renderer to query.

parameters.name: attribute
parameters.description: The attribute of the renderer to query.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Pointer to a variable where the queried value will be stored.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the operation was successful and the attribute is supported, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: win32u_wglQueryRendererStringWINE
function.description: This function queries the renderer string for a given device context, renderer, and attribute. It returns the device name or vendor name based on the attribute provided. If the renderer is not supported or the attribute is not recognized, it returns NULL.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to the device context

parameters.name: renderer
parameters.description: The renderer to be queried

parameters.name: attribute
parameters.description: The attribute to be queried, can be either WGL_RENDERER_DEVICE_ID_WINE or WGL_RENDERER_VENDOR_ID_WINE

function.return_type: char pointer, represents the device name or vendor name based on the attribute provided. Returns NULL if the renderer is not supported or the attribute is not recognized.

function.name: win32u_wglQueryCurrentRendererIntegerWINE
function.description: This function queries the current renderer integer for a given attribute and stores the result in the provided value pointer. It iterates over the devices until it finds the current device. If the device is found, it calls another function to get the renderer integer. If the device is not found, it logs a warning and returns FALSE.

parameters.name: attribute
parameters.description: This parameter represents the attribute for which the renderer integer is being queried.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: This is a pointer to a GLuint where the result of the query will be stored.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the function was able to successfully query the renderer integer. Returns TRUE if successful, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: win32u_wglQueryCurrentRendererStringWINE
function.description: This function queries the current renderer string for a given attribute. It iterates through the devices until it finds the one that matches the current display device. If it finds a match, it returns the renderer string for that device. If it doesn't find a match, it warns the user and returns NULL.

parameters.name: attribute
parameters.description: This parameter represents the attribute for which the renderer string is being queried.

function.return_type: char. It represents the renderer string for the current device if found, otherwise NULL.

function.name: display_funcs_init
function.description: This function initializes the display functions, sets up the pixel formats, and registers various extensions. It also handles error checking for the initialization of the driver OpenGL functions and the allocation of memory for pixel formats.
function.return_type: void, this function does not return any value

function.name: __wine_get_wgl_driver
function.description: This function gets the WGL driver for a given device context and version, and initializes the display functions if necessary. It returns a pointer to the display functions if successful, otherwise it returns NULL.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to the device context.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Version of the WGL driver.

parameters.name: null_funcs
parameters.description: Pointer to the opengl_funcs structure.

function.return_type: struct opengl_funcs. It represents the OpenGL functions that the WGL driver provides.
